cards.hearing: You may be hearing about a bomb plot that was stopped near a U.S. air base in England, and that Iran is denying any role in it.
cards.why: Stories like this can feel scary because they touch on war and security, and that uncertainty is part of why oil and stocks can wobble a bit this week.
cards.but: But headlines like this have happened before, and markets have a long track record of digesting scary news without it changing your long-term plan.
cards.story: Picture checking a storm forecast for a city far from home. You watch it, you note it, but you do not cancel your own week because of weather somewhere else. Distant events get watched, not overreacted to.
say: We see the headline, we are not changing your plan because of it.
Geopolitical scares happen. Your plan is built to ride through them.

cards.hearing: You may be hearing that the government just approved new mileage rules for cars, ending the old electric vehicle requirement from a few years back.
cards.why: That matters because it can change what new cars cost and which models get built, so it can shape your next trip to the dealership.
cards.but: But the plan we built for you doesn't ride on which cars roll off the line or how many miles they squeeze from a gallon.
cards.story: Picture two neighbors. One keeps redoing their household budget every time a new car rule comes out. The other just gets an oil change, waits for their car to actually need replacing, and moves on with their week.
say: We built your plan to handle policy changes like this one.
A new mileage rule doesn't rewrite your long-term plan.
